findings.claim: The introduction of verdict='warn' creates a consumer misinterpretation risk for the 023C aggregator: a downstream implementation that checks 'verdict == "allow"' (allow-list style) would treat 'warn' as non-compliant, while one that checks 'verdict != "deny"' (deny-only style) would treat 'warn' as fully compliant. Neither collapse is correct. The schema enum is explicit (["allow","deny","warn"]) but carries no normative consumer-handling requirement.
findings.evidence: schemas/scorecard-emit.schema.json line 54: verdict enum ["allow","deny","warn"]. policy-check.yml Build scorecard emit heredoc lines 1369-1379: verdict assigned 'warn' when only warn-baseline rules have raw_findings > waived and rule_config_disabled is false. The workflow's 'Render deny annotations and enforce threshold' step (lines 952-1038) does NOT block merge for warn-baseline findings — so verdict='warn' semantically means 'gate passed, SCP-R-004 has raw findings'. An aggregator checking 'verdict == "allow"' treats 'warn' as non-compliant (over-alert); one checking 'verdict != "deny"' treats 'warn' as compliant (under-alert). The schema description ('allow if no effective denies; deny if any effective deny; warn if only warn-baseline rules fired') is accurate but does not specify required consumer handling. The 023C aggregator is not yet built; no existing consumer to assess.
findings.impact: If 023C is implemented with an incomplete three-value handler, cross-repo dashboards could misrepresent repos with SCP-R-004 findings as either fully compliant or non-compliant. Since scorecards are observational (plan-doc invariant 1), there is no gate-bypass consequence. The risk is informational-accuracy degradation in the aggregator's reporting layer.
findings.mitigation: Add a normative consumer-handling note to schemas/scorecard-emit.schema.json's 'verdict' description: 'warn' is a distinct posture (warn-baseline alert; gate passed) that must not be collapsed into 'allow' or 'deny' by the aggregator. File as TF-023C-001 for the 023C aggregator design brief. No 023B runtime change required — this is a forward design constraint. Do not descope.

findings.claim: WARN_BASELINE_RULES is now defined as a Python literal set in two separate heredocs within policy-check.yml: line 973 (Render deny annotations and enforce threshold step) and line 1309 (Build scorecard emit step). A future change that adds a new warn-baseline rule to one heredoc but not the other produces a permanent split-brain: the threshold step and the scorecard emitter disagree on which rules are warn-baseline. No runtime assertion, test, or schema validation prevents this desync.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml line 973: WARN_BASELINE_RULES = {"SCP-R-004"} (threshold step heredoc). policy-check.yml line 1309: WARN_BASELINE_RULES = {"SCP-R-004"} (Build scorecard emit heredoc). The comment at line 1305 acknowledges the mirroring relationship ('Mirrors the WARN_BASELINE_RULES set in the workflow's render-deny step'). No test in tests/scorecard-emit/ asserts parity between the two sets. Desync direction A (emitter adds SCP-R-NNN before threshold step does): threshold blocks merge on SCP-R-NNN deny, emitter reports verdict='warn' — false-negative in scorecard, aggregator under-reports non-compliance. Desync direction B (threshold step adds SCP-R-NNN before emitter does): threshold allows merge, emitter reports verdict='deny' — false-positive in scorecard, conservative.
findings.impact: Neither desync direction creates a gate bypass: the threshold step (which actually blocks merge) remains authoritative regardless. Impact is scorecard misreporting. Direction A (false-negative) is the more dangerous variant: an aggregator consuming verdict='warn' would not escalate a repo that is genuinely blocking merges. Direction B is conservative and self-correcting at the next emitter update.
findings.mitigation: At minimum, add a test that asserts the two WARN_BASELINE_RULES sets are identical (e.g., parse policy-check.yml and compare both occurrences). Preferred fix: promote to a data-driven manifest at policies/rule-baselines.yaml consumed by both steps, eliminating the dual-maintenance surface (TF-020P-001 forward-compat candidate, already referenced in the line 969 comment). File as TF-023B-004. No 023B blocking change required — severity is MIN — but should be addressed before a second warn-baseline rule lands.

self_reported_concerns: WARN_BASELINE_RULES literal integrity (R3 verification point 1): CONFIRMED SAFE. Both occurrences of WARN_BASELINE_RULES = {"SCP-R-004"} (lines 973 and 1309) are Python literals inside single-quoted <<'PY' heredocs. Single-quoted heredoc delimiters disable all shell expansion; the Python interpreter receives the literal bytes {'SCP-R-004'}. No workflow input, environment variable, or adopter-controlled string can inject additional members at runtime. Mutation requires a CODEOWNERS-gated PR on .github/workflows/policy-check.yml. The tamper-to-suppress-a-deny path is bounded by the governance control that already protects the entire workflow. No regression from R1/R2.

Verdict='warn' schema conformance and consumer risk (R3 verification point 2): The schema enum ["allow","deny","warn"] is explicit and the verdict description is accurate. A conforming consumer MUST handle all three values. The risk (R3-MIN-SAFE-001) is a forward design constraint for the 023C aggregator, not a 023B runtime bypass. Scorecards are observational (plan-doc invariant 1): no gate-bypass consequence exists regardless of how a consumer interprets the verdict.

Invariant 2 upheld in both files.
